findings.evidence: Criterion c2: "published" requires the maintainer to publish a release identifier for this board and the version to copy it; a page publishing no release identifier supports "snapshot" with version snapshot-<date>. Neither SOURCE 1 (page excerpt) nor SOURCE 2 (leaderboard.json) publishes any release identifier: leaderboard.json metadata contains only last_updated "2026-09-27" and total_tasks 102, and the string "opt1-102" appears nowhere in either source. The version copies nothing the maintainer publishes, so version_status "published" is contradicted; "snapshot" is the supported value.
findings.repair: Set version_status to "snapshot" and version to a "snapshot-<date>" identity (e.g., snapshot-2026-11-08, the capture date). Alternatively, if a maintainer release identifier is asserted, copy that identifier verbatim into version; no such identifier exists in the supplied sources.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 changelog includes "2026-09-27: Improved elicitation to explicitly ask models to keep measuring and improving after their first speedup", and SOURCE 2 ingests four runs dated 2026-09-27 (Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol) under this identity. The notes document the 2026-04-27 iteration-budget and 2026-07-12 network-isolation changes but omit the 2026-09-27 elicitation change. Criterion c1 requires that a changed configuration not silently reuse the identity; the disclosure gap leaves the newest configuration change undocumented even though new runs under it are included.
findings.repair: Add the 2026-09-27 elicitation change ("explicitly ask models to keep measuring and improving after their first speedup") to scoring.notes alongside the existing 2026-04-27 and 2026-07-12 entries, so all changelog configuration changes affecting ingested runs are disclosed.

uncertainties: I cannot execute hash recomputation or transport/qualification checks; the owner performs those separately. Source transcriptions and the owner-computed per-row sha256 were accepted as packet data for field-level comparison.

Row description ("real codebase", "make the code as fast as an expert developer's optimization") paraphrases the page text ("a codebase... improve runtime efficiency to match an expert developer's optimization"); judged a consistent wording approximation, not an error.
Whether metadata.last_updated could be construed as a release identifier is ambiguous, but even under that reading the version "opt1-102" does not copy it, so F1 stands either way.

Unit "percent" and range [0,100] were judged only against SOURCE 4's admissible summary (32 finite values, min 0, max 88.24); all served values fit the stated bounds, so no mismatch was reported on this point.
SOURCE 4's count of 32 values matches the 32 Opt@1 rows in SOURCE 2; the 2 Opt@10 rows are a separate protocol per the version_guard and were correctly excluded from this identity.
status "active" is supported by SOURCE 3 (4 added score values), and superseded_by null is uncontradicted because no protocol text names a successor board.
